subject: Data lifecycle carveout for GovLogic pilot — next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@govlogic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Data lifecycle carveout for GovLogic pilot — next steps

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed path forward so we all have the same view.

Summary from today's call:
- GovLogic needs a small pilot to validate inference accuracy for classification workflows against live inputs, but the data classification team requires strong controls: 0-retention for PII input, short-lived operational logs, and US-only residency for model execution.
- Procurement needs an ops-friendly mutual action plan (MAP) and a short SOW for the pilot.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Ephemeral input handling mode (0-retention for model inputs) for the pilot. This strips request bodies after inference but preserves aggregated metrics for debugging.
- Short operational log window configurable by customer (we recommended 24 hours during pilot).
- US-only execution via our us-east private tenancy; we can commit to region routing for the pilot.
- Optional pseudonymization layer: we can apply token-level hashing/pseudonymization before entering long-term logs.

Tradeoffs / open items we discussed:
- 0-retention mode prevents us from producing per-request debug traces that contain original PII; that limits some debugging workflows. We recommended a lightweight audit tracer that captures request IDs and anonymized error contexts.
- SOC 2 evidence: we can share our SOC 2 report and the minimal design doc for ephemeral handling, but GovLogic will need to confirm whether that is sufficient for your compliance team.

Attachments: GovLogic_Data_Lifecycle_Summary.pdf (summary of options) and a draft pilot SOW (redwood-ephemeral-pilot-sow.docx).

Proposed next steps (suggested MAP):
1) GovLogic security to review our SOC2 and ephemeral design doc (we'll upload tonight).
2) Procurement to review the short SOW and send any redlines by EOD 5/20.
3) Technical kick-off with GovLogic infra (30–45m) — propose 5/22 or 5/23.
4) Pilot window: 2 weeks with a 24-hr operational log window by default; evaluate moving to 6-hr window if signal is good.

Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether 5/22 works for the technical kick-off?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up.

Jonas Weber

Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle carveout for GovLogic pilot — next steps

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop procurement: 

1) Can Redwood support strict 0-retention for all raw request payloads (no copies), and if so, what debugging alternative do you recommend when we need to triage model regressions?
2) For the short operational logs: can you commit to a hard 24-hour TTL that is reversible only by Redwood engineering under emergency process, or do you rely on customer-configured retention windows?
3) Our security team wants to confirm there are no hidden backups or third-party snapshots that could rehydrate PII; can you provide a short attestation?

Procurement: @procure@govlogic.com is the contact for contracts; they'll expect a short SOW and a one-pager on the tradeoffs for the ephemeral model.

Also propose the tech kick-off on 5/23 at 10:00am PT if that works for your team.

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Data Security
GovLogic Inc.
ellen.park@govlogic.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@govlogic.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle carveout for GovLogic pilot — next steps

Ellen — quick answers to your questions from an implementation standpoint.

1) 0-retention for raw request payloads: yes, we can enable an ephemeral mode where the request body is held only in memory for the duration of inference and never persisted to disk. Implementation notes:
   - Requests are processed in-memory on dedicated containers in our us-east private tenancy.
   - We do store request IDs and lightweight metrics for debugging (latency, error codes). Those metrics contain no PII.
   - For deeper debugging, we offer an opt-in encrypted trace where a customer-designated key encrypts a minimal debug blob; GovLogic can choose to enable it for a small percentage of traffic during the pilot.

2) Operational log TTL: we can enforce a hard TTL policy (24 hours) at the storage layer for the pilot and restrict access via RBAC. Any retention changes require an internal change request and admin approval — we can provide a one-page attestation describing the process.

3) Backups/snapshots: our ephemeral containers are not included in routine backup snapshots. We will provide a short attestation and our infra diagram showing backup scopes.

Risks/notes:
- Enabling encrypted debug traces (even opt-in) introduces storage of small debug blobs; recommend limit usage to <1% of traffic unless GovLogic's security team is comfortable.
- Some integrability features (e.g., per-request trace IDs visible to Redwood console) are limited in 0-retention mode; we can surface aggregated traces instead.

I can join the 5/23 10:00am PT kick-off to walk the infra and controls.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Data lifecycle carveout for GovLogic pilot — next steps

Thanks Ellen — good questions and great timing. TL;DR: Redwood can meet the ask for a strict pilot with 0-retention for PII, a 24-hr log window, and US-only execution. Attached are the SOW and the short attestation Ben referenced.

Concrete next steps (action owners):
- GovLogic security: review attached attestation and infra scope doc (Ellen). Target: feedback by 5/20.
- Procurement: review SOW (Procurement). Target: redlines by 5/20 or flag required legal review.
- Technical kick-off: 5/23 10:00am PT — Ben will demo architecture and ephemeral handling; Neha will cover onboarding and test data patterns.
- Pilot run: 5/26–6/08 (2 weeks). Default operational log TTL: 24 hours; if GovLogic confirms, we can test a 6-hour TTL in week 2.

If procurement wants a short contract wrapper for the pilot (2-week SOW + standard T&Cs), we'll push a DocuSign link by EOD today and can accelerate.

Attachments: redwood-ephemeral-pilot-sow.docx; GovLogic_Data_Lifecycle_Summary.pdf

Looking forward to moving this forward — let us know if procurement would like a call before 5/20.
